title: Security posture discovery with AstraNova Financial
next_steps: Send SOC2+ISO evidence bundle and network diagrams (Sanjay)
Share OIDC/SAML SSO integration guide and SAML metadata (Maya)
Schedule in-depth Dedicated vs Private benchmark with infra team (Ellen/Rahul) - target next week
action_items: Sanjay: attach SOC2 Type II report + ISO 27001 summary by 2026-08-22
Maya: provide SAML/SSO onboarding doc and example metadata by 2026-08-21
Lena: provide list of compliance gates and minimum encryption requirements by 2026-08-25
summary: Discovery focused on AstraNova's security and compliance requirements for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key topics: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and IdP integration, RBAC and granular audit logs, KMS/encryption options, data residency and retention policies. Customer is highly regulated financial firm; primary blockers are encryption keys control and fine-grained auditability.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-20 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Redwood: Sanjay Patel, Maya Li | Customer: Ellen Park (CTO), Rahul Sharma (Head of Security), Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng)
transcript:
[00:00:02] Sanjay Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:00:10] Ellen Park: Hi Ellen here, CTO at AstraNova, we focus on payments infra, happy to be here.
[00:00:14] Rahul Sharma: Rahul, Head of Security. Lots of compliance questions, but want to keep it practical.
[00:00:18] Lena Ortiz: Lena on platform, I'll own the integration work.
[00:00:26] Sanjay Patel: Great, I'm Sanjay AE at Redwood, and Maya our SE will cover technical stuff.
[00:00:29] Maya Li: hi all, quick wave.
[00:00:35] Sanjay Patel: Agenda: we'll do a security posture run-down, talk about hosted/dedicated/private options, and then action items. Sound good?
[00:00:42] Ellen Park: yep.
[00:00:48] Rahul Sharma: good.
[00:01:10] Maya Li: so first question for you Rahul: what are your must-haves from a security/compliance perspective?
[00:01:22] Rahul Sharma: Must-haves: SOC2 Type II, ideally ISO 27001, SSO with our IdP (we use Okta, SAML), ability to control KMS keys or bring-your-own-key, RBAC for role separation, retention and immutable audit logs for 7 years, and data residency in our US region. Also need proof of pen tests and vulnerability scanning cadence.
[00:01:45] Sanjay Patel: Got it. We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO 27001 attestation, we can share the reports. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated — hosted allows BYOK via cloud KMS in certain plans, we'll clarify.
[00:02:05] Rahul Sharma: Can hosted give us full KMS control? We want to ensure keys never leave our control.
[00:02:11] Maya Li: hosted has BYOK integrations with AWS KMS and GCP KMS using customer-managed CMEK, but we do not do HSM-backed BYOK in the multi-tenant hosted unless there's a specialized enterprise contract. For Dedicated and Private you can have HSM/KMS in your VPC or on-prem.
[00:02:30] Ellen Park: So hosted is ok for their less sensitive workloads, but for payment flows we probably need Dedicated or Private. What about audit logs? We need per-request logs with identity and token mapping.
[00:02:43] Maya Li: We emit detailed audit logs including request metadata, model used, tokens, latencies, and the identity that made the call — we map tokens to user/service accounts. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog/S3/CloudWatch or stored in our secure logging service with retention controls.
[00:03:00] Rahul Sharma: Retention controls — can we force immutability / WORM for 7 years?
[00:03:07] Maya Li: For Dedicated and Private yes we can support write-once retention via your storage layer; hosted has retention controls and exportability but true WORM is available as an add-on or via integrating with your compliant storage.
[00:03:20] Lena Ortiz: Ok, integration wise we'll need SAML metadata and a test tenant. Do you support IdP-initiated SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[00:03:28] Maya Li: Yes we support SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning groups and users. We can share sample SP metadata and a SCIM endpoint example.
[00:03:36] Ellen Park: Great. On RBAC, can we do fine-grained roles per route/model, not just org/admin?
[00:03:42] Maya Li: Yes — our RBAC supports roles at the project and route level, and you can bind to groups from SCIM. There are prebuilt roles (admin, developer, auditor) and you can create custom roles with model-level permissions.
[00:04:00] Rahul Sharma: How about key handling in the runtime? If we do Dedicated, is the model serving process able to access KMS keys directly in our VPC?
[00:04:08] Maya Li: In Dedicated and Private deployments the runtime is deployed inside your network and calls your KMS endpoints. For Hosted, we integrate with your cloud KMS but the key never leaves your KMS; the service does call the KMS for decrypt operations in a controlled way. There are architecture diagrams we will share.
[00:04:24] Sanjay Patel: quick callout — we do a security review pack with architecture, pen test summary, SOC2 reports, and network diagrams. We'll attach those after the call.
[00:04:33] Ellen Park: Please do. Also need a list of sub-processors and where data is stored.
[00:04:37] Sanjay Patel: We'll include sub-processor list and regional data residency commitments.
[00:04:45] Rahul Sharma: What about logs for debugging — do you redact PII by default?
[00:04:50] Maya Li: We have configurable redaction and tokenization. By default we redact sensitive fields and provide a policy-driven approach — you can set which fields are persisted.
[00:05:03] Lena Ortiz: Are there any agent level or system-level hostnames leaked in logs? We need network isolation for dedicated.
[00:05:09] Maya Li: For Dedicated and Private, logs only contain customer-facing routing and request metadata; internal hostnames can be stripped. We'll work with your ops to ensure log schemas meet your requirements.
[00:05:24] Rahul Sharma: How do rollouts work? We need canary deploys and automatic fallback to a lower-tier model if latency spikes. That affects audit and observability.
[00:05:33] Maya Li: Rollouts support canary and A/B with traffic split per route. We have tracing hooks and deterministic trace IDs so you can follow a request across model variants. Automatic fallback policies are configurable. All events are logged for audit.
[00:05:50] Ellen Park: On data retention for model caching — do you cache prefixes or KV caches that could contain customer data?
[00:05:58] Maya Li: Default is ephemeral KV cache tied to a session and TTLs. For production you can disable persistent caching or opt into encryption at rest for caches. In Private you can control cache storage.
[00:06:12] Rahul Sharma: What's your default encryption at rest and in transit?
[00:06:17] Maya Li: TLS 1.2+ in transit; encryption at rest with AES-256. We support CMEK for cloud providers and HSM-backed keys for Private.
[00:06:27] Ellen Park: Pen tests — do you have a recent third-party pentest?
[00:06:30] Sanjay Patel: Yes, annual third-party penetration tests and internal red team; we'll include summary and remediation timelines in the packet.
[00:06:38] Lena Ortiz: For Private deployments, what's the deployment packaging and how invasive is it to our infra?
[00:06:44] Maya Li: Private comes as a containerized stack with an operator for your cluster, minimal host-level changes, and documented network ports. We can do an on-prem appliance for air-gapped if required.
[00:06:55] Rahul Sharma: Ok. For SOC2 evidence, will you provide control narratives and test results or just the final report?
[00:07:02] Sanjay Patel: We provide the Type II report and a control map; for enterprise we provide control narratives and evidence bundles under an NDA.
[00:07:10] Ellen Park: Do you support industry standard SIEM ingestion? We use Splunk and Sumo.
[00:07:15] Maya Li: Yes, Splunk, Sumo, Datadog, and native CloudWatch exporters. We also offer a Kafka sink for high-throughput log export.
[00:07:24] Lena Ortiz: Good. On SSO we need SCIM to auto-provision groups and remove access when someone leaves. Is there a deprovisioning webhook?
[00:07:32] Maya Li: We support SCIM deprovisioning and can call your webhook on lifecycle events for immediate revocation.
[00:07:40] Rahul Sharma: For legal, what does your DPA and data processing addendum cover around sub-processor notification?
[00:07:46] Sanjay Patel: Standard DPA with sub-processor list and notification windows; we can add contractually agreed SLAs for notification.
[00:07:55] Ellen Park: Do you offer an encrypted logging option where logs are stored encrypted with our key, separate from the runtime keys?
[00:08:02] Maya Li: Yes, we can configure log encryption with a dedicated key in your KMS for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports export to your encrypted bucket as well.
[00:08:13] Lena Ortiz: Any specific client-side libraries or SDKs we should avoid for PCI scopes?
[00:08:18] Sanjay Patel: We'll share guidance; generally we recommend server-side proxying requests and not embedding secrets in client apps to limit card data surface.
[00:08:28] Rahul Sharma: On breach notification timelines, what's Redwood's commitment?
[00:08:32] Sanjay Patel: Standard 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents, and we do quarterly security updates. We can add specific incident response SLAs into enterprise contract.
[00:08:43] Ellen Park: What's the typical time to complete an attestation review with your security team? We may want a deep dive.
[00:08:49] Maya Li: Usually 2-3 weeks for an initial security questionnaire turnaround, faster if we have an NDA in place and we can schedule a deep dive with our Security Architect.
[00:09:00] Lena Ortiz: For Dedicated, what's the network egress model — do you support private peering and no public internet egress?
[00:09:06] Maya Li: Yes, Dedicated can be configured in a VPC with private peering and NAT restrictions; Private on-prem obviously has no public egress unless you configure it.
[00:09:18] Rahul Sharma: We need to confirm data residency — which regions do you guarantee?
[00:09:22] Sanjay Patel: We have regional deployments in US, EU, and APAC. We can guarantee US-only storage based on your contract and route traffic accordingly.
[00:09:31] Ellen Park: About model artifacts — are models stored encrypted at rest and can we restrict model downloads?
[00:09:37] Maya Li: Model weights and artifacts are encrypted at rest. For Private and Dedicated you control access; hosted does not permit model download but you can pin model versions and control who can call them.
[00:09:50] Lena Ortiz: Do you retain prompts or user data used for improving models?
[00:09:55] Sanjay Patel: By default Redwood does not use customer data to train models unless you opt in. We can add contractual clauses to disallow training data usage.
[00:10:07] Rahul Sharma: Can we get a dataflow diagram of where data moves and what subsystems touch it?
[00:10:12] Maya Li: Yes we'll attach a dataflow diagram showing boundary, encryption points, and KMS interactions.
[00:10:20] Ellen Park: On telemetry, can you send only meta telemetry and no payloads?
[00:10:25] Maya Li: Telemetry is configurable; you can opt out of payload telemetry and only send anonymized metrics.
[00:10:34] Sanjay Patel: quick check — what timeline are you working with?
[00:10:38] Ellen Park: We're doing vendor selection this quarter, procurement and legal loop in early next quarter. We want a pilot in staging within 4-6 weeks.
[00:10:46] Sanjay Patel: Great. A pilot in staging is doable — we typically spin up a Dedicated pilot or a Private eval depending on needs.
[00:10:54] Lena Ortiz: For the pilot, we'll want a config that mirrors production network and KMS so the test is meaningful.
[00:11:01] Maya Li: Understood, we'll propose a staging Dedicated with your KMS integration for the pilot.
[00:11:08] Rahul Sharma: Any blockers regarding compliance frameworks we should know about?
[00:11:12] Maya Li: Not for finance beyond the items we've discussed; we can escalate any specific audit questions to our compliance team.
[00:11:22] Ellen Park: Ok, let's talk about proofs — can you run a simple latency/cost benchmark for our wallet flow pattern?
[00:11:28] Sanjay Patel: Yes, we can run benchmarks against a pinned model with your sequence length distribution and share a cost/latency analysis.
[00:11:36] Lena Ortiz: We'll send representative prompts and traffic patterns.
[00:11:39] Sanjay Patel: perfect.
[00:11:44] Rahul Sharma: From a legal perspective, we may want indemnities for data breach if it's due to Redwood subprocessor. Is that negotiable?
[00:11:51] Sanjay Patel: Standard carve-outs apply, but we can discuss indemnity language with legal if needed.
[00:11:57] Ellen Park: Final question — do you support hardware isolation for inference (dedicated GPUs per tenant)?
[00:12:03] Maya Li: Dedicated pools provide isolated GPU pools reserved to your account, and Private on-prem gives full hardware isolation.
[00:12:10] Lena Ortiz: How about monitoring and observability hooks into our existing prometheus?
[00:12:15] Maya Li: We export Prometheus metrics and provide Grafana dashboards; also tracing integrations are available.
[00:12:22] Sanjay Patel: ok, we'll summarize next steps now.
[00:12:27] Sanjay Patel: ACTIONS: we'll send SOC2+ISO reports, SAML metadata, and dataflow diagrams. Redwood to propose pilot config and benchmark plan.
[00:12:35] Ellen Park: Thanks, that works.
[00:12:38] Rahul Sharma: Good, thanks.
[00:12:41] Lena Ortiz: thanks.
[00:12:44] Sanjay Patel: We'll follow up with the packet and set a follow-up for the pilot kick-off.
[00:12:49] Maya Li: I'll own the SSO doc and lab setup.
[00:12:53] Sanjay Patel: Great. End meeting.
[00:13:00] [meeting end — short administrative hold music in recording]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings; timestamps are approximate. The conversation continued offline for clarifications and a subsequent thread for legal/contract questions.
